SMTO-EXE-0015 — SMTO couldn't bring back the step that was blocked

GUID: 932fd97b-d074-4af8-b839-a9c63d7f9e04
Slug: resource-reconciliation-candidate-unavailable
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • Your task was waiting for another job to let go of something it needed. SMTO couldn't restore the waiting step to run it, and it has not rerun anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Expand the task in the conversation and check which steps finished before it got blocked. Finished steps keep their changes, so the new task should only ask for what's left.
  2. Start a new task in the conversation that asks for just the remaining work. The waiting step can't be restored, but a new task plans that work again from the way things are now.
  3. If the new task is blocked by the same job, use the recovery card in that task to wait or to end the blocking job. The other job may still be holding what your step needs.

What success looks like

  • The new task runs the remaining work and finishes.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't assume the blocked step ran; it was never restarted.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Resource recovery could not proceed because the unsatisfied prerequisite has no retained recovery candidate: the historical operation could not be reconstructed for a run that could not resume normally.

What this means

  • Recovery could not construct or retain an eligible candidate for the requested historical operation in a run that could not resume normally. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • Recovery could not construct or retain an eligible candidate for the requested historical operation in a run that could not resume normally.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the current run's resumability, retained candidate and blocker information rather than reconstructing an operation from a display row.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the run's prerequisites entry for the source_operation (no candidate) and the current resource blockers; the historical operation was not replayed. Continue the work in a new task, or settle the original effects separately; do not fabricate a candidate.
  • Inspect current resource blockers and select an available authoritative recovery candidate.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The owning recovery flow presents an authoritative current candidate or the original effects are settled separately.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
